subject.title: improve(gateway): tunable control-plane write rate limit, default unchanged

question: Should OpenClaw expose a global gateway setting that raises the control-plane write budget for every authenticated identity, or retain the fixed security limit until a trust-scoped design is available?
rationale: Both designs are mechanically feasible, but choosing how operators may weaken this security boundary and whether the new core config surface is worth its long-term contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Close pending sponsorship
options.body: Keep the fixed 3-per-minute limit and revisit the request only when a maintainer sponsors a defined security and configuration policy.

options.title: Approve the global knob
options.body: Accept the bounded setting as an intentional operator-controlled weakening applying uniformly to every gateway identity.

options.title: Request trust-scoped quotas
options.body: Replace the global setting with a narrower credential, identity-class, or automation-specific quota after defining the authorization contract.

recommendation.title: Close pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the fixed 3-per-minute limit and revisit the request only when a maintainer sponsors a defined security and configuration policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing limiter and its security hardening trace to this owner, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the policy decision.
